python3 /tmp/swe/edit.py --create .github/workflows/prepare-release.yml <<'EOF'
name: Prepare Release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to set (e.g. 0.1.0)"
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
        with:
          python-version-file: ".python-version"
      - name: Set version
        run: |
          echo "Updating version to ${{ github.event.inputs.version }}"
          # In a real FastAPI project, this might use a tool like bumpversion or edit pyproject.toml
          # Since this is a generic request and I don't have a specific script, 
          # I'll implement a simple sed to update pyproject.toml if it exists.
          sed -i "s/^version = \".*\"/version = \"${{ github.event.inputs.version }}\"/" pyproject.toml
      - name: Commit and push changes
        run: |
          git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config --global user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add pyproject.toml
          git commit -m "Prepare release ${{ github.event.inputs.version }}"
          git push
EOF
